lede.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia's CEO
lede.dek: Nvidia's board named CFO Colette Kress interim chief executive after Huang's abrupt exit, and Congress is now pressing him to testify over a partner executive's alleged China ties.

top10AsOf: List as of Sep 24, 2026 9:15 PM ET

stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia's CEO
stories.move: Nvidia's board said Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and a director effective immediately on Nov. 12. The board named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO; she keeps her finance role while the company searches for a permanent successor. The board also named Harvey C. Jones, a former Synopsys CEO, as Nvidia's first-ever board chair.
stories.why: Huang built Nvidia into the center of the AI boom over more than three decades; losing him without warning raises succession and strategy questions heading into earnings and a fight in Washington over China chip exports.
stories.bear: Nvidia says Kress and the leadership team have the board's full confidence and that operations and product plans continue without interruption; the stock has stayed near record levels this year.
stories.watch: Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results on Nov. 17 at 1:20 p.m. PT, its first earnings call since Huang's exit.

stories.headline: Congress presses Huang to testify on China ties
stories.move: House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast and other House Republicans asked Jensen Huang to brief Congress behind closed doors over his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Nvidia partner Megaspeed whom U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China. Huang is expected to testify before Thanksgiving, Nov. 26; Nvidia was in talks this week with congressional staff over a date and location.
stories.why: The inquiry adds a national-security dimension to Huang's sudden departure and could shape upcoming restrictions on advanced chip exports to China.
stories.bear: Neither Megaspeed nor Alice Huang has been charged with a crime, and China has denied the spying allegation; Nvidia says it has followed export-control rules.
stories.watch: A scheduled date and location for Huang's testimony, expected before Nov. 26.

stories.headline: AMD slides as chip-stock rally reverses
stories.move: AMD shares fell sharply on Nov. 13 in a broad chip-sector reversal that followed Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia's CEO two days earlier. Our pricing data shows AMD closed down 8.8% that day.
stories.why: AMD had rallied as investors rotated out of Nvidia after Huang's exit; the reversal shows how closely chipmakers' stocks are now tied to Nvidia-specific headlines rather than their own results.
stories.bear: AMD's own guidance is unchanged: Su has told investors she expects 2027 revenue growth above 80%, with data-center AI revenue more than doubling.
stories.watch: AMD's next quarterly update for whether its MI400/MI450 chip ramp stays on track.

stories.headline: Broadcom falls with AMD in chip pullback
stories.move: Broadcom shares also fell on Nov. 13 as the same chip-sector reversal that hit AMD spread to other semiconductor names following Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia. Our pricing data shows Broadcom closed down 4.8% that day.
stories.why: Broadcom had been one of the stocks investors rotated into right after Huang's exit, so the Friday reversal erased some of that week's gains.
stories.bear: Broadcom's underlying AI business keeps growing; the company has guided to roughly $115 billion of AI-related revenue in fiscal 2027.
stories.watch: Broadcom's next earnings call for updated AI-revenue guidance.

stories.headline: Dell falls on report of AI server smuggling probe
stories.move: Dell shares fell about 7.6% in afternoon trading on Nov. 13, to roughly $343, after a report that federal investigators are examining AI server manufacturers over alleged smuggling of chips, a story that also weighed on Super Micro Computer and Nvidia that day.
stories.why: Dell depends heavily on AI server sales to data centers, so scrutiny of the AI hardware supply chain hits the stock hard on its own, beyond the broader chip selloff.
stories.bear: No charges have been reported against Dell itself, and the company has guided to about $19 billion of AI server revenue this quarter.
stories.watch: Dell's fiscal third-quarter report, due Nov. 24.

stories.headline: Arm slides as its CEO is floated for Nvidia job
stories.move: Arm Holdings shares fell on Nov. 13 amid the broader chip-sector pullback and reports that Nvidia's board had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas about replacing Jensen Huang. SoftBank, led by Masayoshi Son, controls Arm. Our pricing data shows Arm closed down 4.6% that day.
stories.why: Losing Haas to Nvidia would be a blow to Arm just as it leans on AI-chip demand for growth, and it underlines how unsettled Nvidia's leadership search is.
stories.bear: No change at Arm has been confirmed; the move is based on reports of talks, not an announced decision.
stories.watch: Whether Nvidia names Haas, Kress or an outside candidate as permanent CEO.

stories.headline: Newsmax jumps 31% on surprise profit
stories.move: Newsmax shares jumped 31.4% on Nov. 13, the day after the media company reported a swing to profitability in its third-quarter results, with revenue and earnings per share both beating estimates. Interactive Brokers chairman Thomas Peterffy is one of Newsmax's largest shareholders.
stories.why: The earnings beat came as the midterm elections drove viewership, and analysts tied part of the profit jump to higher cable-affiliate fees.
stories.bear: Newsmax stock has been extremely volatile since its 2025 listing, and a single profitable quarter may not repeat.
stories.watch: Newsmax's next quarterly report for whether the profitability holds.

stories.headline: Larry Page trusts file to sell $148M of Alphabet
stories.move: Three trusts tied to Larry Page filed Form 144 notices after the close on Nov. 12 to sell 253,840 Class A and 253,840 Class C Alphabet shares, worth about $148.3 million combined, through J.P. Morgan Securities. The filings cite a trading plan adopted Nov. 30, 2020.
stories.why: The sale is part of a long-running, pre-arranged plan rather than a new decision, but it is one of the larger Page family filings this year.
stories.bear: A Form 144 is only a notice of intent to sell, not a confirmed trade; the actual amount could differ once Form 4s are filed.
stories.watch: Form 4 filings confirming the completed trade, expected around Nov. 16.

stories.headline: Warren presses Barra over GM's $20B buyback
stories.move: Sen. Elizabeth Warren sent GM chair and CEO Mary Barra a letter dated Nov. 12 criticizing GM's $20 billion stock buyback plan, arguing it enriches executives and shareholders after GM raised prices and laid off or furloughed thousands of workers. Warren urged GM to use an expected roughly $500 million tariff refund for workers and customers instead.
stories.why: The letter adds political pressure to GM's capital-return plans just as the company leans on buybacks to support its share price heading into what it has called a "bumpy 2027."
stories.bear: GM has framed the buyback as a sign of confidence in its business, and the letter carries no legal force on its own.
stories.watch: Whether GM issues a public response to Warren's letter.

stories.headline: Amancio Ortega collects record Inditex dividend
stories.move: Amancio Ortega, who owns 59.29% of Inditex through his holding companies, received the second of two equal installments of Inditex's 2025 dividend this month. Inditex paid a total of €3.234 billion to shareholders for the year, split between May and November 2026.
stories.why: The payout lands as Inditex shares have traded above €60 for the first time, pushing the value of Ortega's stake further into record territory.
stories.bear: Most of the payout simply reflects Ortega's existing 59% stake rather than new wealth creation, and the share price could still give back its 2026 gains.
stories.watch: Inditex's next trading update for whether the stock holds above €60.

quickHits: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser said a new Chinese securities license completes the bank's product lineup there and gives it an edge over rivals.
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said the crypto industry should "decentralize, but unite," in a Nov. 8 social-media post.
memo: A scandal or personal controversy can remove a star executive overnight — succession plans and clean governance matter even at the top of a boom.
One company's bad headline can hit an entire sector's stock prices, not just its own; know how exposed your business is to a key supplier's or partner's reputation.
Buybacks paired with layoffs invite political scrutiny — plan for that scrutiny alongside the capital-return math, not after the letter arrives.
